N equally spaced charges each of value q , are placed on a circle of radius R . The circle rotates about its axis with an angular velocity $ω$ as shown in the figure. A bigger Amperian loop B encloses the whole circle where as a smaller Amperian loop A encloses a small segment. The difference between enclosed currents, $I_{A}-I_{B}$, for the given Amperian loops is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


The total charge distributed on the circular ring is:

$Q=Nq$

The time taken for one full rotation is:

$T=\frac{2π}{ω}$

The rotating charges create an equivalent circular current given by:

$I=\frac{Q}{T}=\frac{Nq}{\frac{2π}{ω}}=\frac{Nqω}{2π}$

For Amperian loop $A$, the circular current path passes directly through the area bounded by the loop. Therefore, the enclosed current is:

$I_{A}=\frac{Nqω}{2π}$

For Amperian loop $B$, the charges rotate entirely within the plane of the loop and do not cross or thread through the surface bounded by loop $B$. Therefore, the current passing through loop $B$ is:

$I_{B}=0$

Now, finding the difference between the two enclosed currents:

$I_{A}-I_{B}=\frac{Nqω}{2π}-0=\frac{Nqω}{2π}$

text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : An electron in a certain region of uniform magnetic field is moving with constant velocity in a straight line path.

Reason (R) : The magnetic field in that region is along the direction of velocity of the electron. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both $(𝐀)$ and $(𝐑)$ are true but $(𝐑)$ is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to the Lorentz force law, the force experienced by a charged particle, such as an electron, moving in a magnetic field is given by the equation:

$\mathrm{F}–=\mathrm{q}(\mathrm{v}–\times \mathrm{B}–)$

Here, $\mathrm{F}–$ is the force exerted on the particle, $\mathrm{q}$ is the charge of the particle, $\mathrm{v}–$ is the velocity vector of the particle, and $\mathrm{B}–$ is the magnetic field vector. The symbol $\times$ indicates the cross product, meaning the force is perpendicular to both the velocity and magnetic field vectors.

Given this, for the force $\mathrm{F}–$ to be zero:

The velocity $\mathrm{v}–$ and the magnetic field $\mathrm{B}–$ must be parallel (or anti-parallel). This condition will result in the angle $θ=0^{\circ }$ or $180^{\circ }$.

Under these circumstances, the electron will not experience any magnetic force and will continue to move in a straight line with constant velocity, as the cross product becomes zero. Therefore, the reason (R) is indeed a valid explanation: the magnetic field being along the direction of the electron's velocity means no perpendicular force is applied to change its path.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
The magnitude of heat exchanged by a system for the given cyclic process ABCA (as shown in figure) is (in SI unit) :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Step 1: Find the Work Done ($\mathrm{W}$) in the Cycle

The work done in a cyclic process shown in a pressure-volume (P-V) graph is equal to the area enclosed by the cycle. Cycle ABCA is the upper semicircle ABC together with the diameter CA (the lower arc is not part of the cycle), so the enclosed area is that of a semicircle, $\frac{1}{2}πR_{P}R_{V}$, where $R_{P}$ and $R_{V}$ are its semi-axes along the P and V axes.

Step 2: Put in the Given Values

Radius $R$ on the graph is

$R=200 2\times 10 3\text{(for Pressure, P)}\; R=200 2\times 10-6\text{(for Volume, V)}$

Step 3: Calculate the Area (Work Done)

$\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{2}\times π\times \left (\frac{200}{2}\times 10^{3}\right )\times \left (\frac{200}{2}\times 10^{-6}\right )$

First, calculate $\frac{200}{2}=100$, so:

$\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{2}\times π\times 100\times 10^{3}\times 100\times 10^{-6}$

Multiplying $100\times 100=10,000$, and $10^{3}\times 10^{-6}=10^{-3}$, so:

$\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{2}\times π\times 10,000\times 10^{-3}=\frac{1}{2}\times π\times 10=5π\mathrm{J}$

Step 4: Relate to Heat Exchanged

In a complete cycle, the change in internal energy is zero, so total heat exchanged is equal to the total work done.

So, the magnitude of heat exchanged is $5π\mathrm{J}$.

text:
In photoelectric effect, the stopping potential $(\mathrm{V}_{0})\mathrm{v}/\mathrm{s}$ frequency $(ν)$ curve is plotted.

( h is the Planck's constant and $𝜙_{0}$ is work function of metal )

(A) $\mathrm{V}_{0}\mathrm{v}/\mathrm{s}ν$ is linear.

(B) The slope of $\mathrm{V}_{0}\mathrm{v}/\mathrm{s}ν$ curve $=\frac{𝜙_{0}}{\mathrm{h}}$

(C) h constant is related to the slope of $\mathrm{V}_{0}\mathrm{v}/\mathrm{s}ν$ line.

(D) The value of electric charge of electron is not required to determine h using the $\mathrm{V}_{0}\mathrm{v}/\mathrm{s}ν$ curve.

(E) The work function can be estimated without knowing the value of $h$.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Einstein's photoelectric equation with $eV_{0}=K_{\max }$ gives

$eV_{0}=hν-𝜙_{0}\Rightarrow V_{0}=\frac{h}{e}ν-\frac{𝜙_{0}}{e}$

Statement (A): $V_{0}$ is a linear function of $ν$. Correct.

Statement (B): the slope of the line is $\dfrac{h}{e}$, not $\dfrac{𝜙_{0}}{h}$. Incorrect.

Statement (C): since the slope is $\dfrac{h}{e}$, $h$ is found from the slope. Correct.

Statement (D): $h=e\times \text{slope}$, so the electronic charge is needed to find $h$. Incorrect.

Statement (E): extending the line to $ν=0$ gives the intercept $-\dfrac{𝜙_{0}}{e}$ on the $V_{0}$-axis, so $𝜙_{0}=e\times |\text{intercept}|$ is found without $h$. Correct.

Only statements (A), (C) and (E) are correct.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: The energy E and momentum p of a moving body of mass m are related by some equation. Given that c represents the speed of light, identify the correct equation
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each term of the equation must have the dimensions of $E^{2}$, where $[E]=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]$, so $[E^{2}]=[\mathrm{M}^{2}\mathrm{L}^{4}\mathrm{T}^{-4}]$.

With $[p]=[\mathrm{MLT}^{-1}]$ and $[c]=[\mathrm{LT}^{-1}]$:

$[pc]=[\mathrm{MLT}^{-1}][\mathrm{LT}^{-1}]=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}],[mc^{2}]=[\mathrm{M}][\mathrm{L}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]$

Both $pc$ and $mc^{2}$ have the dimensions of energy, so the terms with dimensions of $E^{2}$ are $(pc)^{2}=p^{2}c^{2}$ and $(mc^{2})^{2}=m^{2}c^{4}$, giving $E^{2}=p^{2}c^{2}+m^{2}c^{4}$.

The terms $pc^{2}$ $[\mathrm{ML}^{3}\mathrm{T}^{-3}]$ and $m^{2}c^{2}$ $[\mathrm{M}^{2}\mathrm{L}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]$ in the other options do not have the dimensions of $E^{2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : In an insulated container, a gas is adiabatically shrunk to half of its initial volume. The temperature of the gas decreases.

Reason (R) : Free expansion of an ideal gas is an irreversible and an adiabatic process.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both $(𝐀)$ and $(𝐑)$ are true and $(𝐑)$ is the correct explanation of $(𝐀)$
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let's analyze both statements step by step.

Assertion (A): "In an insulated container, a gas is adiabatically shrunk to half of its initial volume. The temperature of the gas decreases."

 • In an adiabatic process, no heat is exchanged with the surroundings.  

 • For a reversible adiabatic (compression) process, the relationship between temperature and volume is given by  

  $TV^{γ-1}=\text{constant},$  

  where $γ$ is the heat capacity ratio (greater than 1).  

 • If the volume is reduced from $V$ to $V/2$, then  

  $T_{\text{final}}=T_{\text{initial}}\left (\frac{V}{V/2}\right )^{γ-1}=T_{\text{initial}}(2)^{γ-1}.$  

 • Since $(2)^{γ-1}>1,$ the final temperature is higher than the initial temperature.  

 • Therefore, the assertion that the temperature decreases is incorrect.

Reason (R): "Free expansion of an ideal gas is an irreversible and an adiabatic process."

 • In a free expansion, the gas expands into a vacuum without doing any work on the surroundings.  

 • Since the container is insulated, no heat is exchanged, making it adiabatic.  

 • However, the process is inherently irreversible due to the spontaneous expansion and mixing of states.  

 • Thus, this statement is true.

Since Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true (but the reason does not explain the false assertion about temperature change during compression), the correct answer is:

Option C  

(A) is false but (R) is true.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: Young's double slit interference apparatus is immersed in a liquid of refractive index 1.44. It has slit separation of 1.5 mm . The slits are illuminated by a parallel beam of light whose wavelength in air is 690 nm . The fringe-width on a screen placed behind the plane of slits at a distance of 0.72 m , will be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Young's double-slit experiment, the fringe width ($β$) can be calculated using the formula:

$β=\frac{λ^{'}\cdot D}{d}$

where:

$λ^{'}$ is the wavelength of light in the medium,

$D$ is the distance between the slits and the screen,

$d$ is the separation between the slits.

The wavelength in the medium ($λ^{'}$) is given by:

$λ^{'}=\frac{λ_{0}}{n}$

where:

$λ_{0}=690\text{nm}$ is the wavelength of light in air,

$n=1.44$ is the refractive index of the liquid.

Substituting the values,

$λ^{'}=\frac{690\text{nm}}{1.44}\approx 479.17\text{nm}$

Now, convert $λ^{'}$ to meters:

$λ^{'}=479.17\text{nm}=479.17\times 10^{-9}\text{m}$

Next, use the values for $D$ and $d$:

$D=0.72\text{m}$

$d=1.5\text{mm}=1.5\times 10^{-3}\text{m}$

Calculating the fringe width:

$β=\frac{479.17\times 10^{-9}\text{m}\cdot 0.72\text{m}}{1.5\times 10^{-3}\text{m}}$

$β\approx \frac{345.0\times 10^{-9}\text{m}}{1.5\times 10^{-3}\text{m}}$

$β\approx 0.229\times 10^{-3}\text{m}=0.229\text{mm}$

The closest answer choice is:

Option D: 0.23 mm

$\tan θ=\dfrac{|v_{x}|}{|v_{y}|}=\dfrac{20}{5}=4\Rightarrow θ=\tan ^{-1}4$

With the positive $x$-axis the angle is $\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{1}{4}$, not $\tan ^{-1}4$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

In configuration (1) the charges are at the corners of a square of side $a$: four pairs are adjacent (separation $a$) and two pairs are diagonal (separation $\sqrt{2}a$).

$U_{1}=\dfrac{4Kq_{0}^{2}}{a}+\dfrac{2Kq_{0}^{2}}{\sqrt{2}a}=\dfrac{Kq_{0}^{2}}{a}\left (4+\sqrt{2}\right )$

In configuration (2) the midpoints G, E, H, F form a square whose side joins midpoints of adjacent sides, $\sqrt{\left (\dfrac{a}{2}\right )^{2}+\left (\dfrac{a}{2}\right )^{2}}=\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$, and whose diagonals GH and EF equal $a$.

$U_{2}=\dfrac{4Kq_{0}^{2}}{a/\sqrt{2}}+\dfrac{2Kq_{0}^{2}}{a}=\dfrac{Kq_{0}^{2}}{a}\left (4\sqrt{2}+2\right )$

$U_{2}-U_{1}=\dfrac{Kq_{0}^{2}}{a}\left (4\sqrt{2}+2-4-\sqrt{2}\right )=\dfrac{Kq_{0}^{2}}{a}\left (3\sqrt{2}-2\right )$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: The ratio of the power of a light source $S_{1}$ to that of the light source $S_{2}$ is $2$. $S_{1}$ is emitting $2\times 10^{15}$ photons per second at 600 nm . If the wavelength of the source $S_{2}$ is 300 nm , then the number of photons per second emitted by $S_{2}$ is $__________$ $\times 10^{14}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{Since power emitting by a source is given as} \\ \begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{\text{Total energy emitted}}{\text{time}} \\ =\dfrac{(E_{1}\text{photon})\times \text{Number of photons}(N)}{t} \\ P_{1}=(E_{1})n \end{array} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\mathrm{P}_{1}}{\mathrm{P}_{2}}=\dfrac{(\mathrm{E}_{1})\mathrm{n}_{1}}{(\mathrm{E}_{2})\mathrm{n}_{2}}=\dfrac{\left (\frac{\mathrm{hC}}{λ_{1}}\right )\mathrm{n}_{1}}{\left (\frac{\mathrm{hC}}{λ_{2}}\right )\mathrm{n}_{2}} \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{P}_{1}}{\mathrm{P}_{2}}=\left (\dfrac{λ_{2}}{λ_{1}}\right )\dfrac{\mathrm{n}_{1}}{\mathrm{n}_{2}} \end{array} \\ \text{Substituting the given values} \\ \begin{array}{l} 2=\left (\dfrac{300}{600}\right )\times \dfrac{2\times 10^{15}}{\mathrm{n}_{2}} \\ \mathrm{n}_{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 10^{15}=5\times 10^{14}\text{Photon}/\sec  \end{array} \end{array}$

text: The increase in pressure required to decrease the volume of a water sample by $0.2%$ is $\mathrm{P}\times 10^{5}\mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$. Bulk modulus of water is $2.15\times 10^{9}\mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$. The value of P is $_________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The bulk modulus of a material is defined as:

$B=\frac{-\Delta P}{\left (\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right )}$

Given:

Bulk Modulus, $B=2.15\times 10^{9}\text{Nm}^{-2}$

Change in volume percentage, $\frac{\Delta V}{V}=0.2%=\frac{0.2}{100}=0.002$

To find the required increase in pressure, $\Delta P$, we rearrange the formula for the bulk modulus:

$B=\frac{-\Delta P}{-\left (\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right )}$

Plug in the known values:

$2.15\times 10^{9}=\frac{\Delta P}{0.002}$

Solving for $\Delta P$:

$\Delta P=2.15\times 10^{9}\times 0.002$

$\Delta P=4.3\times 10^{6}\text{Nm}^{-2}$

Since the problem specifies $\Delta P=P\times 10^{5}\text{Nm}^{-2}$, we have:

$4.3\times 10^{6}=P\times 10^{5}$

$P=43$

The value of $P$ is therefore 43.

text:
[IMG]


A string of length $L$ is fixed at one end and carries a mass of $M$ at the other end. The mass makes $\left (\frac{3}{π}\right )$ rotations per second about the vertical axis passing through end of the string as shown. The tension in the string is $__________ ML$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The mass moves in a horizontal circle of radius $R=L\sin θ$ with angular speed

$ω=2πf=2π\times \dfrac{3}{π}=6\text{rad s}^{-1}$


[IMG]

The vertical component of tension balances the weight, $T\cos θ=Mg$, and only fixes $θ$. The horizontal component of tension supplies the centripetal force:

$T\sin θ=Mω^{2}R=Mω^{2}L\sin θ$

Cancelling $\sin θ$:

$T=Mω^{2}L=M(6)^{2}L=36ML$

Hence, the answer is 36.

text: Acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is ' $g$ '. If the diameter of earth is reduced to one third of its original value and mass remains unchanged, then the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is $________ g$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ acceleration due to gravity on surface is given by

$\mathrm{g}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}^{2}}$

Now since diameter is reduced to $1/3^{\text{rd}}$, radius also reduces to $1/3^{\text{rd}}$, keeping mass constant

New value of acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface is

$g^{'}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\left (\frac{\mathrm{R}\mathrm{e}}{3}\right )^{2}}=9\frac{\mathrm{GMe}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}^{2}}=9\mathrm{g}$

text:
A tightly wound long solenoid carries a current of 1.5 A . An electron is executing uniform circular motion inside the solenoid with a time period of 75 ns . The number of turns per metre in the solenoid is $_________$.

[Take mass of electron $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}=9\times 10^{-31}\mathrm{kg}$, charge of electron $|\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{e}}|=1.6\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{C}$,

$\left. μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}\frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{A}^{2}},1\mathrm{ns}=10^{-9}\mathrm{s}\right ]$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The problem involves an electron executing uniform circular motion inside a solenoid. The objective is to find the number of turns per meter in the solenoid.

Given:

Current in the solenoid, $I=1.5\text{A}$

Time period of the electron's circular motion, $T=75\text{ns}=75\times 10^{-9}\text{s}$

Mass of electron, $m_{e}=9\times 10^{-31}\text{kg}$

Charge of electron, $|q_{e}|=1.6\times 10^{-19}\text{C}$

Permeability of free space, $μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}\text{N/A}^{2}$

Explanation:

The time period $T$ for a revolving charge in a magnetic field is given by:

$T=\frac{2πm}{qB}$

The magnetic field $B$ inside a solenoid is:

$B=μ_{0}nI$

where $n$ is the number of turns per meter. Thus, substituting $B$ in the expression for $T$, we get:

$T=\frac{2πm}{q(μ_{0}nI)}$

Plugging in the known values:

$75\times 10^{-9}=\frac{(2π)(9\times 10^{-31})}{1.6\times 10^{-19}\times 4π\times 10^{-7}\times n\times 1.5}$

Solving for $n$, we find:

$n=250$

Thus, the number of turns per meter in the solenoid is 250.
